classification.difficultyReason: Reverse depreciation over different periods, interpret the ten-year factor as total percentage loss, and use recovered original value to calculate average annual dollar loss.

content.prompt: Mr Startit’s 10-year-old car is worth $\$6500$, and has been depreciating at $22.5\%$ p.a.

children.label: a
children.prompt: By substituting into $A_n=P(1-R)^n$, find how much (to the nearest dollar) it was estimated to be worth a year ago.

answer.worked:
Here $R=0.225$, so $1-R=0.775$. Let $P$ be the value one year ago.

$$\begin{align*}A_n&=P(1-R)^n\\6500&=P(0.775)^1\\P&=6500\div0.775\\P&\approx\$8387.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How much, correct to the nearest dollar, was it estimated to be worth two years ago?

answer.worked:
Let $P$ be the value two years ago.

$$\begin{align*}6500&=P(0.775)^2\\P&=6500\div(0.775)^2\\P&\approx\$10\,822.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: How much, correct to the nearest dollar, was it estimated to be worth 10 years ago?

children.label: d
children.prompt: What is the total percentage reduction in value on the car over the 10-year period? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
After 10 years, the value is $(0.775)^{10}$ of the original value.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage reduction}&=\left(1-(0.775)^{10}\right)\times100\%\\\text{Percentage reduction}&\approx92.2\%.\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: What was the average reduction in value in dollars per year over the 10-year period? Give your answer to the nearest dollar.

answer.short:
$\$7666$ per year.

Divide the total loss in value by 10.
answer.worked:
Use the unrounded original value from part c.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Total loss}&=\frac{6500}{(0.775)^{10}}-6500\\\text{Average annual loss}&=\frac{6500/(0.775)^{10}-6500}{10}\\\text{Average annual loss}&\approx\$7666\text{ per year}.\end{align*}$$
